### Observed differences

- The relative order of two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, one of A19, A21 and A24 ran before A25 and A29, which in turn ran before A20, A22 and A23 (for example, A25 preceded A20 in about 98 of 100 traces, and A24 preceded A25 in essentially all of the roughly 36 of 100 traces containing both; A19 preceded A20 in about 29 of 100 traces). In the later window every one of these orders is reversed: A20, A22 and A23 precede A25 and A29 in about 97–99 of 100 traces, A25 and A29 precede A19, A21 and A24 (A25 before A24 in about 38 of 100 traces, A24 before A25 in none), and A20 precedes A19 in about 33 of 100 traces while A19 precedes A20 in none. [REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036]
- Event positions moved accordingly: in the later window A19, A21 and A24 sit much later in the trace (median position about 0.35 before, 0.67–0.69 after), while A20, A22 and A23 sit much earlier (median about 0.65 before, 0.38 after); A25 and A29 shift only slightly later. All of these activities ran in essentially every trace in both windows. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- The connections at the edges of the segment moved with it. In the later window A40 leads into A20, A22 and A23 (previously into A21, A19 and A24), and A29 leads into A24, A21 and A19 (previously into A20, A22 and A23). A19, A21 and A24 now run directly into A30 (immediate successor in about 92–97 of 100 observed cases; previously A25 followed in about 93–97 of 100), while A20, A22 and A23 now lead to A25 instead of A30. The gap from A29 to A30 shortened from about four steps to two, and from A40 to A25 it lengthened from about two steps to four to five. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, LAG018, LAG020, LAG021, LAG023, LAG025, LAG026, LAG029]
- A08 is executed far less often: it appeared in about 64 of 100 traces before and about 29 of 100 in the later window (mean occurrences per trace 0.68 → 0.32). When it runs it sits later (mean position 0.26 → 0.41), its immediate succession to A16 largely dissolved (one-step distance in about 99 of 100 observed pairs before, about 43 of 100 after), and A15 is now followed by A16 in about 88 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously about 61, with A08 at about 39). A08's co-occurrence with A14, A15, A16 and the segment activities fell from about 64 to about 29 of 100 traces, the partner now usually running alone. [OCC003, POS001, LAG001, DIR005, REL001, REL005, REL015]
- A04, A06 and A10 run in roughly two to three times as many cases (participation about 7, 7 and 9 of 100 traces before, about 21, 24 and 19 after), and their outgoing transitions now point into the reordered segment (A04 most often to A15, A46 and A23; A10 to A46, A15 and A22) rather than being spread over many other activities. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003]
- Smaller redistributions: A14, A43 and A45 are somewhat less exclusively followed by A15, A44 and A46 (for example A14 to A15 in about 98 of 100 outgoing transitions before, about 80 after), with small new shares towards A04, A06, A08 and A10. [DIR004, DIR014, DIR015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the execution order of a segment was reversed. In the earlier window a case ran one of the alternatives A19, A21 or A24, then A25 and A29, then A20, A22 and A23, and finally A30; in the later window A20, A22 and A23 run first, then A25 and A29, then one of A19, A21 and A24, and then A30 — the middle group kept its place while the two outer blocks exchanged sides. Participation is essentially unchanged for these activities (A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 run together in every trace in both windows; each of A19, A21 and A24 runs in about 29–39 of 100 traces, and the three shares sum to about one per case), so this is a reversal of ordering constraints, not a change in which activities occur. [REL016, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL030, REL031, REL033, POS003, POS005, POS008]

The support is direct and consistent: the pairwise order reversals are near-deterministic in both directions, the positional shifts match them in size and direction, and the successor changes sit exactly at the segment boundaries, with A30 moving from after A20/A22/A23 to immediately after A19/A21/A24. Screening also found 94 qualifying control-flow items where about 1 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the ensemble of differences is not what a stable process typically produces. [REL023, REL024, REL030, REL031, REL033, REL034, POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, DIR006, DIR007, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]

Limitations: the evidence aggregates order shares over whole traces, so it cannot separate a reordering within one flow from a shift in the mix of complete trace variants that contain these activities in different orders — the main competing explanation it cannot rule out. Positions and lags are event positions rather than clock times, so no statement about calendar timing is implied. [REL016, POS002, LAG018]

Other differences:
- A08 participates in far fewer cases (about 64 → 29 of 100 traces) and, when present, sits later, usually no longer directly precedes A16, and precedes the segment less often (A08 before A20 in about 57 of 100 traces before, about 18 after) — a participation change in its own right rather than part of the reorder. [OCC003, POS001, LAG001, DIR005, REL005]
- A04, A06 and A10 are executed about two to three times as often and now feed into the segment. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003]
- Smaller successor redistributions appear at A14, A43 and A45. [DIR004, DIR014, DIR015]
